newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 2-year note coupon rises to 13.75 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 2-year note coupon rises to 13.75 pct.

text.p: The Philippine two-year note coupon rose to 13.75 percent from the previous 11.625, the Bureau of Treasury said on Tuesday.
The lowest bid was at 13.5 percent and the average at 13.638.
The Treasury had offered four billion pesos worth of notes but it received bids worth 3.93 billion.
The auction committee, which took an unusually long 30 minutes to decide on the yields, agreed to accept bids worth only 200 million pesos.
If the committee had accepted all the bids, the highest yield would have been at 17.875 percent, an official of the Bureau of Treasury said.
The levels at which the bids were submitted reflects the market's expectations after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate to a two-year high of 30 percent.
The crucial rate was raised to 30 percent on Monday after the Philippine peso came under attack from speculators.
Since Thailand announced a managed float policy for the baht two weeks ago, a move seen as a de facto devaluation, analysts have said the peso could be the next target as it was overvalued.
The Central Bank has staunchly defended the peso by selling dollars and raising interest rates.
"The rates were too high. There was also the option to reject everything but there were acceptable levels, National Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa told Reuters after the auction.
She said the 30 pct overnight borrowing rate had discouraged banks from investing in T-bills.
"We'll have to review our cash position, our programmes, our borrowings," she said.
